Screen Recording 2025-02-05 at 6.55.00 PM.mov
<https://drive.google.com/file/d/1yfuO995qPXFZThXkW10zHE6JGdbrs335/view?usp=drive_web>

Thanks Nick!  Confirming receipt and attaching the video of us doing an
example labeling task.  This doesn't have audio, but what's happening is
we're moving through this video and hitting "1" "2" "3" "4" etc. to
annotate the video at different timestamps with the language that
corresponds (in the top right) to each of those numbers, also using the
timeline scroller at the bottom.  The annotations get persisted as JSON;
we'd want to know how we'd get those annotations back from you all.

This video is ~3min long--partially because in the absence of audio we sort
of labored over "showing" what's happening.  I'd hope that a similar task
would take an annotator y'all provide less time than that per episode.
Look forward to hearing what you expect this would take!

Initial thoughts, to recap what I told Nick R. as we went long in our
meeting today:
- $25K just to get platform access (but no annotators) for one year is
high, since we already have a tool we can use.  What we're primarily
interested in paying y'all for is speed of onboarding and deploying
annotators--not the platform
- I also notice that there's a 2-year commitment baked into the contract.
We'd prefer not to be committed to that duration of time out of the gate.

Will follow up with a more complete response soon.

Evan

subject: Re: Labeling project
text:
Hi Matt,

I added 5 more videos to show how we caption the segmented motions. In this
labelling project, the 7 categories represent coarse-level action labels,
and the detailed motion descriptions represent the fine-grained motions for
the coarse-level labels.

Regarding the detailed motion description, the principle is to faithfully
describe how the subject does the task. For example, when lifting a box,
the subject can either simply pick up the box from the table without
bending over, or lean forward, stretch his two arms to pick the box up.
These scenarios are very different in our ergonomic assessments so we hope
our model could learn the difference.

Please let me know if you have any questions or concerns. Thanks!

Jun
